items.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: the real troopers like the Dinah Washingtons and the Harry Belafonte and people like that, they were the ones who really suffered with that

ctx.x: What was the impact of the civil rights movement and then the civil rights bill in ’64 or whatever. Did it make any difference in your life?

To tell you the truth I can’t say that it did really. The only thing it could have made a difference was that maybe hotel accommodations or something, but see I didn’t really get caught up in that because the real troopers like the Dinah Washingtons and the Harry Belafonte and people like that, they were the ones who really suffered with that where they could work at a club in any city but they couldn’t stay at the hotel where they worked, or they had to change their clothes in the bus or something. So I really…
